title: All from 9 and the Last from 10

steps.prompt: You pay for a $368$-point item with $1000$ points. How much change? Try it without borrowing.

cards.title: No borrowing
cards.body: To take a number away from $1000$, take each digit from $9$, and the last digit from $10$. $1000 - 368$: $9 - 3 = 6$, $9 - 6 = 3$, $10 - 8 = 2$, so $632$. For $10000$, do the same with four digits.

cards.title: Why it works
cards.body: $1000 = 999 + 1$. Taking a number from $999$ never needs borrowing, because every digit is $9$. Then add the $1$ back at the end, which is the same as taking the last digit from $10$. (It only works when the last digit isn’t $0$.)

prompts: Explain why "all from $9$ and the last from $10$" never needs borrowing.
